To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the change of the bridged halide in a series of tetraamidato-diruthenium compounds allows the study of the magnetic, structural and electrical properties of the resulting compounds.
the first linear paddle-wheel diruthenium compounds that do not show a maximum of magnetic susceptibility towards temperature have been prepared and characterized.

we have prepared a new family of one-dimensional tetramidato diruthenium compounds, which are the first examples with bromide or iodide as bridging ligands and we have studied their structure, their magnetic properties and their electrical conductivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, crystal structures, magnetic and electrical behaviours of a family of new tetraamidato-bridged diruthenium compounds.
the preparation and characterization of new compounds of the type Ru2X(μ-NNC6H4-R-CONH)4 (X = Br, I; R = o-M, m-M, p-Me) using microwave activation procedures.
a systematic study of the structural, magnetic and electrical conductivity properties of the tetraamidato-diruthenium compounds as a function of the nature of the bridging ligand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic behaviour of compounds 1-6 is dominated by the Ru-Br-RuC and Ru-I-RuC angles and not by the nature of the halogen.
the halides play a key role in the properties of these compounds, which is reflected in the different magnetic, structural and electrical properties of the compounds.
the magnetic and electrical properties depend mainly on the nature of the halide ligand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the change in halide ligand from Cl to I in the tetraamidato-diruthenium complexes leads to a decrease in zero field splitting, an increase in antiferromagnetic exchange and an increase in electrical conductivity.
the magnetic properties of these compounds depend on the bridging ligand, whereas their conductivity properties depend on the nature of the halide ligand.
the change of the bridged halide ligand from Br to Cl and I has a strong effect in the magnetic and electrical properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic and electrical properties are not only determined by the nature of the bridging ligands, but also by the nature of other ligands and the geometry of the metal centres.

the change of the bridged ligand in tetraamidato diruthenium complexes from Cl(-) to Br(-) and I(-) leads to a change from linear to non-linear coordination polymers with significant differences in their physical properties.
the halide ligand plays an important role in determining the magnetic properties of the complexes.
